Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in New York, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Saturday, October 24Passed

By mail or online: your application must be RECEIVED by your board of elections by Saturday, October 24, 2026. In person at your board of elections: by Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

By mail: postmarked by Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and received by your board of elections by Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Dropped off in person: before polls close at 9 p.m. on November 3, 2026. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on New York’s own site

At school away from home, in New York or in another state? What New York says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed for an EARLY MAIL ballot, which any registered voter may ask for. New York also still has the ABSENTEE ballot, which does need a reason: being away from your county (or, in New York City, away from the five boroughs) on Election Day; illness or disability; caring for someone ill or disabled; being a resident or patient of a Veterans Health Administration hospital; or being in jail for anything other than a felony conviction. Both are filled in and returned the same way. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Outside New York City: download the early mail ballot application from the State Board of Elections' ballot application site and mail it to your county board of elections. Allow time for mailing. Open it (official page)
  • Online (New York City). New York City voters can request on the NYC Board of Elections' page (also in Chinese, Korean and Bengali). Open it (official page)
  • In person. Apply at your county board of elections. For an absentee ballot, you can have someone else deliver it to the board and bring your ballot to you; write that person's name in the box on the application. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Use the prepaid return envelope. The state warns that a ballot dropped in a mailbox may not be postmarked until the next day or later; to get the postmark the same day, ask for a free hand postmark at a post office. (official page)
  • In person. Drop it off at your county board of elections before 9 p.m. on Election Day; during early voting (October 24 to November 1) at any early voting site in your county (in New York City, in your borough only); or on Election Day at any poll site in your county or borough before 9 p.m. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Put the marked ballot in the security envelope, then sign, date and seal the security envelope, and put it in the prepaid return envelope. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on New York’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, October 24, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Early voting runs Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1, 2026. October 24 is also the last day to register, and you can register and vote that same day. Election Day polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. (official page)

Students

At school in New York, away from home

New York's election law says you do not gain or lose a voting residence just because you are a student somewhere. When deciding, the board of elections looks at what you say you intend and at your circumstances (for example, where you file taxes, where your parents live, a lease, vehicle registration). A student registered at home can ask for an early mail ballot (no reason needed), or an absentee ballot when away from their county on Election Day. (the law)

At school in another state, with New York as home

The state's pages do not speak to students in another state separately. Its general rules: being a student elsewhere does not by itself make you gain or lose a New York voting residence; anyone may vote by early mail ballot; and being away from your county (or, in New York City, the five boroughs) on Election Day is a reason for an absentee ballot. (the law)

Military and overseas

Under New York law a military ballot in a general election counts if it arrives before polls close, or if its envelope has a postmark (or a dated mark from a U.S. agency, or the voter's and one witness's signatures and date) no later than Election Day and it arrives within 13 days after, by Monday, November 16, 2026. (the law)

New York in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • In New York City, track your mail ballot at the NYC Board of Elections' tracker (requestballot.vote.nyc/tracking); outside the city, use the State Board's voter lookup.
  • Problems voting: the Attorney General's election protection hotline, 1-866-390-2992, during early voting and on Election Day.
  • The 13-day window for military ballots is computed here as November 16, 2026; the law gives the rule.

How this was checked

  • The New York State Board of Elections' own website (elections.ny.gov) refused automated reading when this was checked, so this record relies on the state Attorney General's voter pages and the Election Law itself. Links to the Board's own request, tracking and county pages are given as the Attorney General's pages give them.
